correctness.rationale: For rational line L with F_q basis U,V, each Frobenius binomial restricts to its corresponding cross-product coefficient times (s^q t−s t^q). This factors curve|_L as a product of a simple rational-point factor and Q_L, the restriction of (c+kb)X²+aY²+bZ². Q_L is not identically zero: a rank-three ternary quadratic has no 2-plane totally isotropic; rank-two such a plane must contain its radical axis, which fails for L in each parameter case; rank-one gives a nonzero square. Consequently 0,1,2 rational roots of nonzero binary Q correspond respectively to 0 tangencies, a double rational flex of exact contact three, or two rational tangencies. In odd characteristic its discriminant equals −4λ²(a³b+b³c+ac³+k(b⁴+abc²)) via the adjugate identity. Counting each rational point’s unique tangent gives 2B+F=N and counting rational lines gives zero-tangent count E=B, with F=#D_k(F_q), N=q²+q+1. For smooth quartic genus 3 gives Hasse |F−(q+1)|≤6√q, |B−q²/2|≤3√q. Fresh independent direct tangent-gradient tests for five prime fields q=3,5,7,11,13 exactly match quartic F and B. Minor proof typo: the rank-one γ-only line is Y−kZ=0 (source writes Y+kZ=0), but Q_L=bZ² still nonzero in either expression, so theorem and nonvanishing conclusion are unaffected.

value.rationale: The result reduces rational tangent fibers of a high-degree Frobenius plane-filling curve uniformly in q to rational points of a fixed quartic (genus three when smooth), yielding exact three-type incidence census and square-root errors. This is a natural structural arithmetic-geometric bridge rather than an arbitrary finite table or mere restatement of smoothness.
